title: Power Automate desktop flows: encrypt and decrypt files with PGP
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, PGP action details, licensing and documented controls are supported. The assurance about sensitive values staying out of run logs needs qualification for Microsoft's documented logging vulnerability and the premium-account condition.

claims.claim: Desktop flows have a PGP Cryptography action group for encrypting and decrypting files using OpenPGP.
claims.quote: The PGP Cryptography group of actions provides a set of tools for encrypting and decrypting files by using the OpenPGP (PGP) standard.

claims.claim: Encrypt file with PGP encrypts a file using the recipient's public key.
claims.quote: By using these actions, you can protect sensitive files by encrypting them with a recipient's public key.

claims.claim: The public key can be supplied as a file path or ASCII-armored text.
claims.quote: Whether you provide the public key as a file path or as ASCII-armored text.

claims.claim: Decrypt file with PGP decrypts a PGP-encrypted file using a private key.
claims.quote: Decrypt a PGP-encrypted file using a private key and passphrase.

claims.quote: Use these actions to securely exchange files with external systems, business partners, and applications that support PGP encryption.

claims.claim: The encryption algorithm options are AES-128, AES-192, AES-256, Triple DES and CAST5.
claims.quote: | Encryption algorithm | No | AES-128, AES-192, AES-256, Triple DES, CAST5 | AES-256 | The symmetric encryption algorithm to use. |

claims.claim: AES-256 is the default encryption algorithm.
claims.quote: | Encryption algorithm | No | AES-128, AES-192, AES-256, Triple DES, CAST5 | AES-256 | The symmetric encryption algorithm to use. |

claims.claim: The maker can choose a compression algorithm for encryption.
claims.quote: | Compression algorithm | No | None, ZIP, ZLIB, BZIP2 | ZIP | The compression algorithm to apply before encryption. |

claims.claim: The maker can choose whether encrypted output uses ASCII armor.
claims.quote: Wraps the encrypted output in ASCII armor (text format starting with -----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----).

claims.claim: ASCII armor is off by default.
claims.quote: | ASCII armor | No | Boolean | False | Wraps the encrypted output in ASCII armor (text format starting with -----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----). When disabled, the output is raw binary data. |

claims.claim: With ASCII armor disabled, encryption produces raw binary output.
claims.quote: When disabled, the output is raw binary data.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A key hardcoded as text in action properties becomes part of the flow definition.
claims.quote: The desktop flow logs will be protected, but the hardcoded values are visible in the modal and the flow definition in Microsoft Dataverse.

claims.claim: A running PGP flow handles the configured key material and passphrase on its run machine.
claims.quote: The error occurs because direct inputs are encrypted using the local machine's Data Protection API (DPAPI) and can't be decrypted when the flow is run on another machine.

claims.claim: Desktop-flow logs can capture action details.
claims.quote: The input details of the Set variable action aren't visible in the desktop flow logs when the contained variables have been marked as sensitive.

claims.claim: Sensitive-variable values are masked in the flow designer during debugging.
claims.quote: The flow designer masks the values of sensitive variables during debugging, and it doesn't store them in flow run logs.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft documents that sensitive-variable values are not stored in flow run logs.
claims.quote: The flow designer masks the values of sensitive variables during debugging, and it doesn't store them in flow run logs.
claims.fix: Qualify the assurance in the control description and prose: 'Microsoft documents omission of sensitive-variable values from portal Run history when signed in with an organization premium account. Microsoft also documents a logging vulnerability in Power Automate for desktop versions 2.62 through 2.66 when global sensitive variables are used in local subflows; update to release 2.67.143.26090 or later, or a patched earlier release listed by Microsoft.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/power-platform/power-automate/desktop-flows/sensitive-variables-security-update alongside the existing variables reference. That security page documents the exception to the general assurance.

claims.claim: Desktop action-group visibility is enabled in Power Platform admin center at Settings > Tenant settings > Desktop flow actions in DLP > Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies.
claims.quote: On the left side panel, select Settings. / On the Tenant settings page, select Desktop flow actions in DLP. / Turn on Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies, and then select Save.

claims.claim: The printed PowerShell retrieves desktop-flow modules, converts them to id/name/type objects and uses Add-ConnectorsToPolicy to add them to a policy's Blocked group.
claims.quote: id=$modules.id / name=$modules.Properties.displayName / type=$modules.type / Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -Connectors $desktopFlowModulesToAddToPolicy -PolicyName $dlpPolicy.name -classification Blocked -Verbose

claims.where: controls[0].governs; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies provide a general control over desktop-flow modules and their actions.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.where: controls[0].note; summary; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented which DLP module contains the PGP actions, including whether they map to Cryptography.
claims.quote: Searched: "PGP" "DLP" "Power Automate"; opened PGP Cryptography actions and prevent-data-loss, and read desktop-flows/data-loss-prevention search text. Cryptography is listed, but no passage maps the PGP actions to it or another module.

claims.claim: The data-policy reference lists Cryptography but no PGP module.
claims.quote: Searched: "PGP" "DLP" "Power Automate"; read the complete Desktop flow modules in DLP list on prevent-data-loss. It includes DesktopFlow.Cryptography Cryptography but no PGP entry.

claims.claim: Data policies classify modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business or Blocked.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.claim: The Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies setting must be enabled before action groups appear in the policy-creation UI.
claims.quote: By default, desktop flow action groups don't appear when you're creating a DLP policy. You need to turn on the Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies setting in your tenant settings.

claims.claim: That tenant setting cannot be changed after it is enabled.
claims.quote: After this setting is enabled, it can't be changed.

claims.claim: Administrators can use the documented PowerShell route without enabling the desktop-action visibility tenant setting.
claims.quote: If you don't want to turn on the Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies setting, you can use the following PowerShell script to add all desktop flow modules to the Blocked group of a DLP policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Adding desktop-flow modules to data policies causes existing flows to be evaluated and noncompliant flows to be suspended.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: Modules not explicitly placed in a policy group are not blocked even when the default group is Blocked.
claims.quote: Desktop flow modules that aren't explicitly added to any group aren't subject to the default group classification and aren't blocked, even if the default group is set to Blocked.

claims.claim: In the Power Automate for desktop designer, a maker marks a variable sensitive through Variables pane > right-click the variable > Mark as sensitive.
claims.quote: To mark a variable as sensitive, right-click it in the variables pane and select Mark as sensitive.

claims.claim: No documented API or automation operation is provided for the maker's per-variable Mark as sensitive setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop sensitive variable mark as sensitive API PowerShell Dataverse workflow definition; read manage-variables, secure-your-data and the returned search excerpts. No operation or documented request property for this per-variable flag was found.

claims.claim: Mark as sensitive is a maker-side, per-variable setting rather than a tenant-wide setting.
claims.quote: Any variable can become sensitive, independently of its type. Sensitivity applies at the variable level

claims.quote: Searched: "PGP" "Power Automate" "sensitive"; read the entire PGP reference, sensitive-variable documentation and search excerpts. No PGP-specific automatic sensitivity or input-logging behaviour was stated.

claims.claim: Incorrect passphrase is a documented PGP decryption exception.

claims.claim: A sensitive-variable value is visible when sent outside desktop flows.
claims.quote: The value of a sensitive variable is visible when you send it outside desktop flows or display it through the Display message action.

claims.claim: A sensitive-variable value is visible when displayed using Display message.
claims.quote: The value of a sensitive variable is visible when you send it outside desktop flows or display it through the Display message action.

claims.claim: Marking a variable sensitive does not protect sensitive values hardcoded in action properties.
claims.quote: Sensitive variables aren't meant to provide protection over hardcoded data. You shouldn't hardcode critical data in plain text, like passwords and PINs, in the properties of actions like Set variable, even if the said variables are marked as sensitive.
